figures.caption: Figure 1: Architectural bifurcation of sensory restoration. Starting from clinical sensory and motor pathology (such as in late-stage ALS or locked-in state, typified by the patient Anna), clinical interventions split into the invasive pathway (direct surgical implantation of Utah arrays, ECoG grids, or endovascular stents providing high-fidelity, bidirectional pathways) and the non-invasive pathway (scalp EEG/MEG recording and sensory substitution offering scalable, lower-risk communication channels).

Figure 3: Timeline of key invasive speech-BCI milestones from 2015 to 2026. The progression highlights a rapid acceleration in speed and channel count, leading to high-dimensional decoding (Willett et al., 2021) and real-time speech avatar synthesis (Metzger et al., 2023).

Figure 4: Timeline of non-invasive speech-BCI milestones from 2022 to 2026. A notable inflection point occurs in late 2023 with the alignment of electrophysiological signals to self-supervised language representations (Défossez et al., 2023), enabling robust decoding using large language models.
Table 1: Cross-Pathway Technical and Clinical Trade-offs

Figure 5: Visual comparison of cross-pathway trade-offs. The scatter plot maps different BCI modalities along two primary axes: spatial-temporal resolution (representing signal capacity) versus clinical risk and relative system cost. This highlights the trade-offs described in Table 1 and visualizes the physical limits frontier.

Figure 6: Convergence of the two pathways into a closed-loop end state. As clinical and technical maturity increase (left to right), the invasive (red) and non-invasive (blue) pathways progress through their respective near-, mid-, and long-term milestones and converge into a unified hybrid platform. The end state (right) is a closed-loop bidirectional system in which a shared neural–AI model couples efferent decoding of speech and motor intent (sensory-OUT) with afferent cortical microstimulation of S1/V1 (sensory-IN), reconnecting the user (Anna) to both communication and sensation.

Figure 7: BCI convergence roadmap. Development proceeds through three phases: (1) near-term non-invasive communication, (2) medium-term implanted high-density decoders and closed-loop hybrid systems, and (3) long-term true bidirectional restoration, combining S1/V1 microstimulation and speech motor decoding.
